description: Retrieves facts for a file similar to the Linux/Unix stat command.

parameters.name: checksum_algorithm
parameters.description: Algorithm to determine checksum of file. Will throw an error if the host is unable to use specified algorithm. The remote host has to support the hashing method specified, md5 can be unavailable if the host is FIPS-140 compliant. Availability might be restricted by the target system, for example FIPS systems won’t allow md5 use Choices: "md5" "sha1" ← (default) "sha224" "sha256" "sha384" "sha512"

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Whether to follow symlinks. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: get_attributes
parameters.description: Get file attributes using lsattr tool if present. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: get_checksum
parameters.description: Whether to return a checksum of the file. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: get_mime
parameters.description: Use file magic and return data about the nature of the file. This uses the file utility found on most Linux/Unix systems. This will add both stat.mimetype and stat.charset fields to the return, if possible. In Ansible 2.3 this option changed from mime to get_mime and the default changed to true. Choices: false true ← (default)

parameters.name: get_selinux_context
parameters.description: Get file SELinux context in a list [user, role, type, range], and will get [None, None, None, None] if it is not possible to retrieve the context, either because it does not exist or some other issue. Choices: false ← (default) true

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The full path of the file/object to get the facts of.

examples:
# Obtain the stats of /etc/foo.conf, and check that the file still belongs
# to 'root'. Fail otherwise.
- name: Get stats of a file
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: /etc/foo.conf
  register: st
- name: Fail if the file does not belong to 'root'
  ansible.builtin.fail:
    msg: "Whoops! file ownership has changed"
  when: st.stat.pw_name != 'root'

# Determine if a path exists and is a symlink. Note that if the path does
# not exist, and we test sym.stat.islnk, it will fail with an error. So
# therefore, we must test whether it is defined.
# Run this to understand the structure, the skipped ones do not pass the
# check performed by 'when'
- name: Get stats of the FS object
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: /path/to/something
  register: sym

- name: Print a debug message
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "islnk isn't defined (path doesn't exist)"
  when: sym.stat.islnk is not defined

- name: Print a debug message
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "islnk is defined (path must exist)"
  when: sym.stat.islnk is defined

- name: Print a debug message
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "Path exists and is a symlink"
  when: sym.stat.islnk is defined and sym.stat.islnk

- name: Print a debug message
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "Path exists and isn't a symlink"
  when: sym.stat.islnk is defined and sym.stat.islnk == False


# Determine if a path exists and is a directory.  Note that we need to test
# both that p.stat.isdir actually exists, and also that it's set to true.
- name: Get stats of the FS object
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: /path/to/something
  register: p
- name: Print a debug message
  ansible.builtin.debug:
    msg: "Path exists and is a directory"
  when: p.stat.isdir is defined and p.stat.isdir

- name: Do not calculate the checksum
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: /path/to/myhugefile
    get_checksum: no

- name: Use sha256 to calculate the checksum
  ansible.builtin.stat:
    path: /path/to/something
    checksum_algorithm: sha256

return_values.name: stat
return_values.description: Dictionary containing all the stat data, some platforms might add additional fields. Returned: success

return_values.name: atime
return_values.description: Time of last access Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 1424348972.575

return_values.name: attributes
return_values.description: list of file attributes Returned: success, path exists and user can execute the path Sample: ["immutable", "extent"]

return_values.name: charset
return_values.description: file character set or encoding Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats and installed python supports it and the get_mime option was true, will return unknown on error. Sample: "us-ascii"

return_values.name: checksum
return_values.description: hash of the file Returned: success, path exists, user can read stats, path supports hashing and supplied checksum algorithm is available Sample: "50ba294cdf28c0d5bcde25708df53346825a429f"

return_values.name: ctime
return_values.description: Time of last metadata update or creation (depends on OS) Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 1424348972.575

return_values.name: dev
return_values.description: Device the inode resides on Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 33

return_values.name: executable
return_values.description: Tells you if the invoking user has execute permission on the path Returned: success, path exists and user can execute the path Sample: false

return_values.name: exists
return_values.description: If the destination path actually exists or not Returned: success Sample: true

return_values.name: gid
return_values.description: Numeric id representing the group of the owner Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 1003

return_values.name: gr_name
return_values.description: Group name of owner Returned: success, path exists, user can read stats, owner group can be looked up and installed python supports it Sample: "www-data"

return_values.name: inode
return_values.description: Inode number of the path Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 12758

return_values.name: isblk
return_values.description: Tells you if the path is a block device Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: ischr
return_values.description: Tells you if the path is a character device Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: isdir
return_values.description: Tells you if the path is a directory Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: isfifo
return_values.description: Tells you if the path is a named pipe Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: isgid
return_values.description: Tells you if the invoking user’s group id matches the owner’s group id Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: islnk
return_values.description: Tells you if the path is a symbolic link Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: isreg
return_values.description: Tells you if the path is a regular file Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: true

return_values.name: issock
return_values.description: Tells you if the path is a unix domain socket Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: isuid
return_values.description: Tells you if the invoking user’s id matches the owner’s id Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: lnk_source
return_values.description: Target of the symlink normalized for the remote filesystem Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats and the path is a symbolic link Sample: "/home/foobar/21102015-1445431274-908472971"

return_values.name: lnk_target
return_values.description: Target of the symlink. Note that relative paths remain relative Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats and the path is a symbolic link Sample: "../foobar/21102015-1445431274-908472971"

return_values.name: mimetype
return_values.description: file magic data or mime-type Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats and installed python supports it and the get_mime option was true, will return unknown on error. Sample: "application/pdf; charset=binary"

return_values.name: mode
return_values.description: Unix permissions of the file in octal representation as a string Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: "1755"

return_values.name: mtime
return_values.description: Time of last modification Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 1424348972.575

return_values.name: nlink
return_values.description: Number of links to the inode (hard links) Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 1

return_values.name: path
return_values.description: The full path of the file/object to get the facts of Returned: success and if path exists Sample: "/path/to/file"

return_values.name: pw_name
return_values.description: User name of owner Returned: success, path exists, user can read stats, owner name can be looked up and installed python supports it Sample: "httpd"

return_values.name: readable
return_values.description: Tells you if the invoking user has the right to read the path Returned: success, path exists and user can read the path Sample: false

return_values.name: rgrp
return_values.description: Tells you if the owner’s group has read permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: true

return_values.name: roth
return_values.description: Tells you if others have read permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: true

return_values.name: rusr
return_values.description: Tells you if the owner has read permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: true

return_values.name: selinux_context
return_values.description: The SELinux context of a path Returned: success, path exists and user can execute the path Sample: ["user", "role", "type", "range"]

return_values.name: size
return_values.description: Size in bytes for a plain file, amount of data for some special files Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 203

return_values.name: uid
return_values.description: Numeric id representing the file owner Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: 1003

return_values.name: version
return_values.description: The version/generation attribute of a file according to the filesystem Returned: success, path exists, user can execute the path, lsattr is available and filesystem supports Sample: "381700746"

return_values.name: wgrp
return_values.description: Tells you if the owner’s group has write permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: woth
return_values.description: Tells you if others have write permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: false

return_values.name: writeable
return_values.description: Tells you if the invoking user has the right to write the path Returned: success, path exists and user can write the path Sample: false

return_values.name: wusr
return_values.description: Tells you if the owner has write permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: true

return_values.name: xgrp
return_values.description: Tells you if the owner’s group has execute permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: true

return_values.name: xoth
return_values.description: Tells you if others have execute permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: true

return_values.name: xusr
return_values.description: Tells you if the owner has execute permission Returned: success, path exists and user can read stats Sample: true
